subject: general
question: A dishonest shopkeeper pretends to sell his goods at cost price, but uses a false weights and gains 11(1)/(9)\%. For a weight of a kg, he uses:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit % = 11(1/9)% = 1/9 in **fractional form**.

This means for every 9 units of **False Weight**, the profit is 1 unit.

Ratio of **True Weight** to **False Weight** = (9 + 1) : 9 = 10 : 9.

Given 10 units = 1000 gm (1 kg).

⇒ 1 unit = 100 gm.

⇒ 9 units = 9 × 100 gm = 900 gm.

**∴ The correct answer is 900 gm weight.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Profit percentage** = 11(1/9)% = 100/9%

**True Weight** = 1 kg = 1000 gm

**Formula Used:**

Profit % = [ (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight ] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1fbf023fa0563088f4273acbed710f433a5273a4b62e09eaf392ae05f68e4558.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **False Weight** used by the shopkeeper be x gm.

⇒ 100/9 = [ (1000 − x) ÷ x ] × 100

⇒ 1/9 = (1000 − x) ÷ x

⇒ x = 9 × (1000 − x)

⇒ x = 9000 − 9x

⇒ 10x = 9000

⇒ x = 900 gm

**∴ The correct answer is 900 gm weight.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer sells at **Cost Price** but uses less weight, the **Profit %** is always calculated on the **False Weight** (what he actually gives).

Case of Dual Profit

If a dealer marks up the price by a% and also uses a false weight giving b% less, the **Total Profit %** = [ (100 + a) / (100 − b) × 100 ] − 100.

Successive Percentage Method

For cheating while buying (x%) and selling (y%), the **Net Profit %** can be calculated using the formula: x + y + (xy/100).</p
